title: Starvation
body:
A [[Processes|process]] starves when it is permanently ready to run and never gets picked.
Nothing is broken, nothing has crashed, the system is making progress; it is just always
someone else's progress.

Starvation is the failure mode [[Bounded Waiting]] exists to rule out. Bounded waiting says
time in the entry section has an upper bound, and a bound on waiting time is exactly the
statement "you will eventually get in".

Where it comes from:

- **Strict [[Process Priority|priority]] scheduling.** High-priority work keeps arriving,
  the low-priority process is always second in line. Fixed by *aging*: raise a process's
  priority the longer it waits.
- **Unfair lock release.** A [[Semaphores|semaphore]] that wakes an arbitrary waiter rather
  than the longest-waiting one can leave one thread never chosen. A [[FIFO]] [[Wait Queue]]
  fixes this, which is why wait queues are FIFO.
- **[[Spin Lock]] contention.** Whoever happens to test the flag at the right instant wins;
  an unlucky thread can lose repeatedly.

## Not the same as deadlock

Worth keeping straight, because the words get used loosely:

| | Starvation | Deadlock |
|---|---|---|
| Is anyone making progress? | yes, just not you | no, everyone involved is stuck |
| Can it resolve on its own? | yes, if the load changes | no, never |
| Cause | scheduling policy | a cycle of processes each holding what another needs |

The vault has no deadlock note; it is a logged content gap for this course.
